page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.large is an entry-tier instance within the vendor's compute-optimized family, running on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources consist of two dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon 8163 core operating at 2.5 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 2.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network performance is anchored by a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no local storage devices, requiring reliance on attached network block storage, and offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reflects entry-level throughput constrained by the single physical core allocation. In synthetic processing assessments, the instance generated a stress-ng single-core score of 1098.29 and a multi-core metric of 1457.69, placing overall CPU performance in the lower percentiles. Memory benchmarks indicate cached read bandwidth of 81.39 GB/s against uncached read and write speeds of 10.26 GB/s and 9.37 GB/s, respectively. Workload evaluations demonstrated 1.43 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.77 GB/s static web serving capacity, alongside modest LLM inference results of 37.46 generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

Resource constraints dictate narrow operational boundaries. The low memory volume of 2.0 GB restricts concurrency and precludes memory-intensive databases, data warehousing, or large language models. However, the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent instruction execution without burst credits or shared core throttling, offering cost-effective execution for deterministic compute jobs. The instance is suited for lightweight microservices, monitoring agents, basic CI/CD utility steps, low-traffic static web servers, and automated scripting workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.large is a compute-optimized virtual server engineered for entry-level computational requirements. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, the x86_64 KVM instance delivers two dedicated vCPUs across one physical core with two threads, backed by 2.0 GB of system memory and 35 MB L3 cache. The instance features no bundled local storage, requiring external volumes for persistence, and maintains a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps without bundled public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark performance aligns with its compact core count, demonstrating 1457.69 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 1.43 million operations per second in Redis SET trials. Because the 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio limits larger in-memory processes, the instance functions with high cost efficiency in lighter service roles, including lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, background processing queues, and edge utility scripts.
